title: Snuffling Cat
desc: Chronic feline upper respiratory / rhinosinusitis — Cerenia for congestion, pulse-dosed azithromycin, famciclovir, saline flushing, and the supportive protocol (Mandelker).

meds.name: Cerenia
meds.desc: the best drug on this sheet for nasal congestion
meds.doseText: ¼ to ½ of a 16 mg tablet
freqs: twice daily for 1–2 days, then once daily for 5 days
meds.note: Then drop to a maintenance dose of 2 to 4 mg per cat twice weekly, or a low dose daily, or a regular dose every other day. Works by blunting the excess substance P in the area, which is what drives the discharge and inflammation. (Lester Mandelker)

meds.name: Cerenia in a nebuliser
meds.doseText: 2 drops of injectable Cerenia in the nebuliser saline
meds.note: Reported on this sheet to have worked very well in one cat, with the owner noting improvement right away.

meds.name: Azithromycin tablets
meds.desc: anti-inflammatory and anti-biofilm as much as antibiotic
freqs: once daily for 5 days, then twice weekly
meds.note: The twice-weekly phase continues for weeks to months. (Lester Mandelker)

meds.name: Azithromycin liquid
freqs: once daily for 5 days, then every 3 days (or twice weekly) for 6 weeks
meds.note: 10 mg/kg. The suspension is 50 mg/ml, so divide the milligrams above by 50 to get the volume in ml. (Folger)

meds.name: Famciclovir
meds.doseText: 62.5 mg twice daily, or 250 mg once daily
meds.note: Published doses are all over the map, up to 40 mg/kg TID. The two regimens above are what this sheet settles on, depending on the consultant.

meds.name: Nasal saline flush
meds.doseText: a saline nasal flush (or hypertonic saline 2–3%)

meds.name: Neo-Poly-Dex drops
meds.desc: ophthalmic drops used intranasally after flushing
meds.note: Hold the head back so the drops run backward.

meds.name: Chlorpheniramine
meds.desc: antihistamine that is synergistic with Cerenia
meds.doseText: chlorpheniramine at your usual feline dose
meds.note: Also mildly antidepressant — roughly 50% of the anti-anxiety effect of fluoxetine — while keeping antihistamine effects that work synergistically with Cerenia. No dose is given on the source sheet.

meds.name: Krill oil capsules
meds.doseText: a krill oil capsule per label

meds.name: Adequan, then oral GAGs
meds.desc: aims at repairing cartilage damage in the sinuses
meds.doseText: Adequan as directed, then oral GAGs
meds.note: Intended to improve cartilage damage and repair in the sinuses left behind by previous viral and bacterial damage.

meds.name: High-protein, gluten-free diet
meds.doseText: a high-protein, gluten-free wet food — no dry food
meds.note: High glucose and high carbohydrate diets have more pro-inflammatory effects. The sheet is emphatic: NO DRY FOOD.

notes.Source: The numbered protocol on this sheet is from Lester Mandelker, DVM, DABVP, Fellow AAVPT.
notes.Order of attack: 1) pulse-dosed azithromycin as an anti-inflammatory and anti-biofilm; 2) local therapy — saline or hypertonic saline flush followed by ophthalmic drops; 3) Cerenia for congestion and substance P; 4) chlorpheniramine alongside it; 5) krill oil; 6) Adequan then oral GAGs; 7) antioxidants; 8) a high-protein gluten-free diet with no dry food.
notes.Why Cerenia: Much of the congestion and discharge in these cats is driven by excess substance P in the nasal tissue, which is what maropitant blocks — this is why it outperforms decongestants here.
notes.Long game: These are weeks-to-months protocols, not a one-week course. The maintenance phases (azithromycin twice weekly, Cerenia twice weekly) are the part that keeps cats comfortable.

dischargeBlocks.title: What we are treating
dischargeBlocks.text:
{name} has long-standing inflammation in the nose and sinuses. In most cats this started with a virus years ago and left the lining permanently damaged, so bacteria and inflammation settle in easily.

We are aiming to keep {name} comfortable and breathing freely. This is managed over months rather than cured in a week — please do not be discouraged if it takes a while.

dischargeBlocks.title: Why the medication schedule changes
dischargeBlocks.text:
Some of these medicines start daily and then drop to twice a week. That is deliberate, not a mistake or a taper.

Please follow the dates on the labels, and keep giving the twice-weekly doses even when {name} seems well — that is what stops the snuffles coming back.

dischargeBlocks.title: If we asked you to flush the nose
dischargeBlocks.text:
Tip {name}'s head gently backward so the drops or flush run toward the back of the nose rather than straight out.

Expect sneezing afterwards — that is the point, it clears the discharge out.

dischargeBlocks.title: Food
dischargeBlocks.text:
Please feed a high-protein, wet food and stop dry food altogether. Dry food is high in carbohydrate, and that seems to make the inflammation worse.

Warming the food slightly makes it smell stronger, which helps a blocked-up cat keep eating.

dischargeBlocks.title: Call us if
dischargeBlocks.text:
- {name} stops eating for more than a day
- The breathing becomes noisy at rest, or open-mouthed
- There is bleeding from the nose
- One side only becomes affected, or the face looks swollen or asymmetrical

A cat that cannot smell its food will often stop eating, and that needs attention quickly.

dischargeBlocks.title: Follow up
dischargeBlocks.text: Please book the recheck we discussed so we can see how far the congestion has settled and decide how long to keep the maintenance doses going.
